Please read /papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/fixed_coefficient_parameter_geometry/E02_R10_VERIFICATION_AND_MODEL_HANDOFF_20261030.md, and continue with B03 R11: a different signed-source mechanism with an explicit domain and complete error payment. It remains unstarted; global coverage remains unresolved.

Track your progress in the research progress folder, write research notes in the notes folder, and record chat history in the chat-histories folder. Please provide guidance for the continuation at the end of your research, and a continuation note for model changes.
I’ll read the handoff and repository workflow, then work through B03 R11 and record the results, remaining gaps, and continuation guidance in the investigation folders.

The handoff confirms the key boundary: the finite tube is accepted, but widening its unchanged error budget fails. R11 needs a different source estimate, with any denominator and every remainder paid independently. This is a new chat, so I’m preserving its own history identity.

The repository already has substantial work on high-height Riemann–Siegel estimates, including limits on their absolute error payments. I’m checking a different option: a finite Hermite–Gaussian approximation built from the complete signed source. It offers explicit oscillatory terms and a complete residual; the question is whether its error can remain small relative to its first jet at unbounded height.

This candidate has a useful, precise test. A paired Gaussian gives an oscillatory leading term whose first jet stays nonzero through its simple zeros. But theta’s source decays faster than every Gaussian, so Hardy’s uncertainty theorem prevents any fixed finite Gaussian approximation from keeping a uniformly small relative error at unbounded height. I’m checking the normalization and full residual payment before recording that scoped failure.

The obstruction now covers the true signed remainder, not just a loose error bound. On \(31/128\le T\le33/128,\ A\ge64\), every fixed finite Gaussian-packet model must fail a uniform relative-error comparison somewhere arbitrarily far out. Finite windows and models that change with height remain outside this result. I’m finishing the checks and the assessment handoff.

The research note, self-review, progress update, and model-change handoff are saved. The exact constant checks, file links, and eight frozen assessment inputs pass verification. E02 R11 is ready for a separate assessment; global coverage remains unresolved. I’m refreshing the chat history before the final handoff.

B03 R11 is complete as a **scoped negative result**, with author checking only.

On \(31/128\le T\le33/128,\ A\ge64\), I derived an explicit oscillatory Gaussian-source model and complete error payment. Applying [Hardy’s uncertainty theorem](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.1543v1) shows that fixed finite Gaussian models cannot maintain uniform relative first-jet accuracy at unbounded height. Finite windows and adaptive models remain outside this exclusion.

- [Continuation and model-change handoff](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/fixed_coefficient_parameter_geometry/B03_R11_RETURN_AND_MODEL_HANDOFF_20261030.md)

Chat history is registered as **0052**. Next is **E02 R11**, with Sol recommended, followed by a non-Gaussian or justified adaptive mechanism. **Global coverage remains unresolved.**
Can you describe at a high level what the results have shown so far?
I’ll review the current progress record and separate the established results from the remaining global gap.

The work has established **a rigorous local noncollision method and several precise limits on extending it globally**. The global argument remains open.

1. **We can distinguish an ordinary zero from a collision.** At a simple zero, \(H=0\) but its slope \(H_A\) is nonzero. A collision requires both to vanish. Studying them together lets the method remain meaningful as it passes through ordinary zeros.

2. **That method now works for the actual theta source on a whole finite region.** For
   \[
   T=\tfrac14\pm\tfrac1{128},\qquad 64\le A\le66,
   \]
   R9 establishes exactly one simple zero at each time, with the slope uniformly separated from zero. This covers a continuous region and includes complete error bounds for the infinite source. It is more than a collection of sampled checks. [R9 research note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/fixed_coefficient_parameter_geometry/B03_R9_SIGNED_SOURCE_TRANSPORT_20261030.md)

3. **The auxiliary flow preserves a quantitative consequence of that separation.** R10 supplies one common flow coefficient and a positive energy floor for every auxiliary time on the certified tube. The important dependency is that the source estimate supplies noncollision first; the flow then carries that information forward. “Every auxiliary time” does not enlarge the range of physical heat times.

4. **We know why simply pushing the same approximation farther fails.** Earlier rounds improved local error payments and reduced the degree needed for some certificates. But R10 shows that widening the unchanged transport budget to \([64,68]\) necessarily loses its positive certificate. This diagnoses the estimating method; it says nothing adverse about theta at height 68.

5. **R11 identifies a stronger limitation of a different approximation family.** Fixed finite Gaussian-source models have explicit oscillatory leading terms and complete error bounds, but their true errors cannot remain uniformly small relative to the relevant first jet at unbounded height. Better evaluation alone cannot repair that fixed family. Finite windows, adaptive families, and non-Gaussian models remain possible. [R11 research note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/fixed_coefficient_parameter_geometry/B03_R11_FIXED_GAUSSIAN_SOURCE_RELATIVE_OBSTRUCTION_20261030.md)

The remaining difficulty is **controlling signed cancellation at the scale of the actual field as height and physical time vary**. A positive source or a well-behaved auxiliary flow does not by itself prevent cancellation. We still need that global source estimate, its coverage argument, and the transfer to the RH/Newman target.

R9 and R10 have internal cross-model assessments. R11 currently has author checking only; its separate assessment is next.

Please include the most recent results in the manuscript, any results that are not already included, and try to maintain a methodical development of ideas, focusing on analytic results with numerics treated as support. Can you then describe the major bottlenecks to controlling cancellation at larger heights, what types of methods have been tried and ruled out, and if there are any particularly challenging aspects that I could help try to troubleshoot?

I’ll audit the manuscript against the research notes, integrate the missing results in a coherent analytic sequence, and check the resulting build. Then I’ll explain the main cancellation bottlenecks, the precise scope of the methods ruled out, and the questions where your input could help most.

I’m using the PDF skill to check the manuscript’s final rendering. I’ll keep the analytic arguments in the main development, place numerical certificates in a supporting role, and preserve the distinction between assessed results and R11’s still-pending assessment.

The audit found several missing pieces: the R6–R11 remainder and approximation results, the earlier Poisson-localization obstruction, and the prepared-source tail result. I’ll place each where its prerequisites are developed, so the manuscript explains why the next method was tried. The finite certificates will support those arguments in the numerical appendix.

The main obstacle is becoming clearer: the known estimates can bound the complete source very accurately in absolute terms, but those bounds can still exceed the small quantity left after cancellation. The manuscript will distinguish this loss of accuracy from an actual failure of noncollision, and state which versions of each method the obstruction rules out.

A useful positive result now belongs in the main development: the method certifies a whole rectangle containing a simple-zero curve, rather than only isolated neighborhoods where \(H\) stays positive. The newer obstruction results explain why that success cannot be extended merely by widening the same Taylor calculation or keeping one finite Gaussian model at all heights.

The updated manuscript compiles successfully, and all 47 earlier proof blocks are preserved. I’m checking the new sections against their source notes and assessment records now. I’m also writing a continuation note that separates promising questions about signed cancellation from approaches already ruled out in a specific form.

The clearest troubleshooting opportunity is to control the leading contribution and remainder together. A remainder can be large and constructive; a bound that insists it must be small can fail even when the full jet is well separated from zero. I’ve documented this alongside the separate obstacles involving simple-zero crossings, moving source tails, and coverage as physical time approaches zero.

The manuscript and research records are updated, and the source checks pass. R11’s separate assessment is still the next task; global coverage remains unresolved. The compiler succeeded, but access to the app’s preview was denied, so I’ve recorded that final pagination and page layout remain unchecked.

I updated and successfully compiled the [manuscript](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/radial_deformations_and_zero_dynamics.tex), incorporating the missing Poisson-localization results, R6–R11, and the prepared-source tail obstruction. Analytic arguments lead the development; numerical certificates support them in the appendix. All 47 earlier proofs are preserved. **R11 remains explicitly marked as awaiting separate assessment.**

The strongest recent positive result is a certified rectangle near \(T=1/4\), with \(64\le A\le66\), containing a simple-zero curve. Although \(H\) crosses zero, \(H_A\) stays separated from zero, so the pair \((H,H_A)\) never vanishes there. That independently established margin also gives a common-flow energy floor for every auxiliary time. This remains a finite physical region.

**The central bottleneck at larger heights is preserving accuracy relative to the small quantity left after cancellation.** We can rigorously bound the complete source and every discarded contribution, yet the resulting absolute error can exceed the signed signal. More precision cannot repair an error allowance that is mathematically too large.

Several specific approaches have now been ruled out:

| Approach | Established limitation |
|---|---|
| Fixed radius and fixed degree with absolute remainder bounds | The prescribed allowance eventually overwhelms the available margin. Adaptive choices remain open. |
| Widening the existing order-17 Taylor transport | Its error payment already fails on \([64,68]\), even with perfect polynomial range bounds. This says nothing adverse about the actual theta jet there. |
| Absolute primitive or Poisson-mode estimates | The tested primitive bounds cost more than their matched direct bounds; absolute Poisson-mode costs grow enormously while the complete source remains integrable. |
| One fixed finite Gaussian source model | R11 shows that its true error cannot remain uniformly small relative to the model or physical jet throughout an entire height tail. |
| Pointwise nonpositive mixed production | The actual prepared source has a positive far tail. Its integrated sign remains unresolved. |
| Positivity, carrier shape, and unsigned flow estimates alone | Colliding controls share these properties, or the estimates already depend on the physical nonvanishing they would need to prove. |

Two further obstacles remain: estimates must stay useful through simple zeros, and eventual coverage must handle height together with physical time approaching zero. A succession of successful finite rectangles does not establish either requirement.

**Your most useful troubleshooting contribution would be to identify a relation that controls the complete signed interaction.** In particular:

- Can theta’s exact coefficient and phase relationships control the leading contribution and remainder together? A large remainder may be constructive; requiring it to be small can discard useful information.
- Is there a natural adaptive or non-Gaussian reference whose amplitude can be bounded independently and whose two-component comparison stays regular through simple zeros?
- Can the integrated feedback identity couple its quadratic error and mixed term strongly enough to pay the positive tail without assuming the desired mass margin?

I saved the detailed [bottleneck analysis](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/fixed_coefficient_parameter_geometry/32_HIGH_HEIGHT_CANCELLATION_BOTTLENECKS_AND_TROUBLESHOOTING_20261030.md) and [continuation/model-change note](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/05_radial_theta_collision_geometry/notes/fixed_coefficient_parameter_geometry/33_CONTINUATION_AFTER_E03_R2_AND_MODEL_HANDOFF_20261030.md), updated progress, and arranged chat-history capture. The next bounded task is E02 R11 assessment; global coverage remains unresolved.

Compilation passed, but preview access was denied, so final page layout remains unchecked.
